overview: Cahokia was a major Mississippian center near the Mississippi River in present-day Illinois. Monumental earthworks, neighborhoods and public spaces preserve evidence of organized labor, farming and exchange.

items.text: Builders accumulated earth in repeated construction stages to create Monks Mound. Its terraces supported a monumental focus for the settlement.
Different mound forms served different purposes, including platforms for public buildings and places of burial.
A circular arrangement of wooden posts known as Woodhenge functioned as an astronomical observatory.
Residential and specialized activity areas formed a wider settlement around the monumental core. Agriculture and trade supported its population.
Cahokia's material record includes figurines and effigy pottery. The site's educational kit uses replicas of these objects to explore Mississippian symbolism.
Cahokia represents one major center within the much wider Mississippian cultural tradition. The city and the entire tradition should have distinct records.
